title: Claim decomposition map
summary: This intermediate resource records that the existing guide cannot yet be safely corrected because its current text, prior revision, and replacement first-party source were not supplied. It identifies the evidence needed to make a source-move or review-cadence correction without rewriting unaffected material.
prerequisites: The prior revision or diff for the resource
The old citation and its authoritative replacement, or the prior verification record
Access to the catalogue schema and identifier index

sections.title: Practitioner answer
paragraphs: Can you correct the cited-source change now while preserving the rest of the guide? UNKNOWN. Do not publish a substantive correction from the supplied record. The current guide, its prior revision, the old and replacement citations, and evidence of a successful source check are absent, so neither the changed source nor the affected claims can be established.

The only citation identified is the local path content/resources/research-verification/claim-decomposition-map.json, attributed to an unregistered publisher and never verified. This does not establish whether a publication moved or merely reached a review deadline. It also provides no directly resolving HTTPS publication to place in the final source list. The affected content is therefore UNKNOWN and no claim-level correction is made.
sections.callout: Intermediate level: preserve the existing resource until the missing evidence supports a narrow, reviewable correction.

sections.title: Blocked correction path
paragraphs: First obtain the complete current resource and its prior revision. If either is unavailable, stop and request both rather than reconstructing text. Next obtain the old citation and an authoritative replacement if the source moved, or the previous verification date and applicable review interval if only a scheduled review triggered the work. If these records are unavailable, record the trigger as UNKNOWN and do not alter substantive claims.

Check each proposed HTTPS source against the publication it is meant to support, including its publisher, title, and relevant content. If a source cannot be checked, do not mark it verified and omit claims that depend on it. Compare the supported change with the prior revision, then edit only the citation and the statements demonstrably affected by that citation. If the comparison cannot isolate the affected statements, stop and request editorial review rather than rewriting the guide.

Before committing, validate the object against the authoritative resource contract and check the shared catalogue for identifier conflicts. If the contract or catalogue is unavailable, do not claim schema conformance or uniqueness. The suggested identifier claim-decomposition-map follows the supplied filename, but matching the actual target path and uniqueness across the catalogue remain UNKNOWN until those records are inspected.
sections.callout: Each failed check has the same safe recovery: stop publication, obtain the missing record or verification evidence, and resume from the failed check.

sections.title: Expected evidence and verification
paragraphs: A completed correction should leave a small diff containing the verified source change and only the text that change affects. Evidence should include the unchanged current resource as a baseline, the prior revision, the former citation, the authoritative replacement or cadence record, successful checks of every final HTTPS source, and validation against the authoritative resource contract and shared identifier index.

Verify the result by comparing it with the baseline and confirming that every changed statement is traceable to the documented source event. Confirm that all unaffected text is byte-for-byte unchanged. Then parse the committed file as one JSON object and apply the platform's authoritative validation process. If parsing, schema validation, source checking, identifier checking, or the baseline comparison fails, do not publish; correct the reported issue or obtain the missing evidence and repeat the failed verification.

This object documents a blocked update rather than claiming the requested guide correction is complete. The changed cited source is UNKNOWN, and its effect is UNKNOWN, because the supplied local path contains neither a verifiable publication nor revision evidence. Replacing the unavailable guide with newly written subject matter would violate the requirement to preserve unaffected material.
sections.callout: Success requires verified provenance and a narrowly scoped diff, not merely valid JSON.
